grades.reason: Covers wait/exit/kill and the ZOMBIE/reparenting mechanics. It never mentions pipes, file descriptors, closing the write end, or EOF, so it doesn't help diagnose a pipe read that never sees EOF.

grades.quote: the kernel code that reads from a pipe calls sleep if the pipe buffer is currently empty; the condition in this case is the pipe buffer becoming non-empty (due to another process writing to the pipe).
grades.reason: Explains that a pipe reader sleeps when the pipe buffer is empty and is woken only when a writer calls wakeup. That helps explain why the reader blocks. It says nothing about EOF or about the write end needing to be closed (for example, by the child or by the reader itself), which is the real cause, so it is only auxiliary.
